title: Prefill Entropy Trimmer & Runtime Sequence Groomer
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: Reduce wasted padding and improve kernel efficiency by introducing an entropy-aware sequence bucketing strategy ("entropy trimmer") that heuristically shortens prefill sequences and groups requests by information density rather than raw token count. This ticket covers design + prototype of the runtime scheduler changes (prefill-decimation policy), integration with kernel selection hints, and a short benchmark harness to validate p50/p95 latency and token-cost reductions. Success criteria: (1) 10-20% reduction in average padding tokens for mixed web-text workloads; (2) <= 3% regression in p50 latency for short/interactive requests; (3) measurable improvement in kernel utilization efficiency on A100/RTX-class nodes when compared to the current length-only bucketer. Constraints: must preserve deterministic output for pinned model versions unless explicitly enabled per-customer; must be opt-in behind a runtime flag and per-route config. Deliverables: design doc (Confluence), prototype in runtime scheduler, kernel-hinting API changes, perf results and open PR(s).
comments: 2026-02-12 - Spike notes: explored information-density heuristics. Two promising lightweight signals: token entropy estimate from byte-level histogram (fast) and lexical surprise via a small subword LM sampled on first N tokens. Entropy estimate chosen for prototype due to speed and memory constraints.

2026-02-18 - Design review: PM + Research reviewed trade-offs. Agreed on multi-step pipeline: 1) cheap entropy estimator at ingress; 2) classify request into compact|normal|long buckets; 3) apply prefill decimation for compact bucket (drop trailing low-entropy segments up to threshold) and route to small-kernel path; 4) emit kernel-hint tag so runtime can pick smaller tile sizes / faster attention kernels. Action: produce confluence doc -> /confluence/rw/prefill-entropy-trimmer (draft).

2026-02-24 - Engineering note: implemented estimator in ingress filter (C++) and an opt-in runtime flag `entropy_trimmer.enabled=true`. Added per-route controls: `trimmer.sensitivity=0.0..1.0` and `trimmer.max_shrink_tokens`. Kept default conservative (0.1 sensitivity, max 32 tokens).

2026-03-03 - Benchmark 1 (mix-traffic-1): baseline avg padding tokens=18.2, after prototype=13.9 => 23.6% reduction. p50 latency change: -1.1% (slightly faster), p95: +2.8% (investigate tail). Observed pathological cases where classifier mislabels templated prompts with repeated boilerplate as low-entropy; added heuristic to detect repeated substrings and skip trimming for templates.

2026-03-06 - Kernel integration: added `kernel_hint: compact_prefill` metadata so kernel selector can choose the smaller-kernel path with reduced KV allocation and alternative attention tiling. Integration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2789

2026-03-10 - Performance profiling: kernel-side savings occur mostly in KV-alloc and attention kernel invocation count for sequences shortened by >16 tokens. On A100, throughput per-GPU improved by ~6% for the compact bucket mix. On RTX, improvement was ~3% due to different memory tiling.

2026-03-12 - QA results: end-to-end determinism tests passed for default (flagged-off) configs. With trimmer enabled, added audit log entries capturing original vs trimmed length for customer review. Security review required? Not for the estimator itself, but customer-data policies reviewed to ensure no leakage via trimming metadata.
notes: Follow-ups: (1) refine entropy estimator to avoid misclassifying templated requests (heuristic added, still under test); (2) add a bounded fallback to ensure p95 tail not regressed for interactive SLAs; (3) explore tighter integration with dynamic kernel-selection heuristics to expose tiling choices to the scheduler via `kernel_hint_score`. Also schedule a canary on Dedicated region us-west-2 for a low-traffic customer segment.
